annotations.text: Surface 1 — Candidate picker, drawn on a wishlist Leica M6. Reuses 002's sheet chrome (background fill, 12px top radius, grabber, medium/large detents, Cancel/title bar). The new work is Phase B's image-first grid.

Image-first: a 2-column square-crop grid (aspect-fill, clipped to a square, 2px radius). The photo IS the choice, so it's large; the credit stays secondary. This is a single Leica M6 query — a real search returns one gear type, so the variety here is framing/background/quality, plus a couple of near-misses (a lens, a light meter).

Surface 2 — How a stored stock photo is marked and credited everywhere it appears: a STOCK PHOTO badge over the hero, a quiet credit line ending in a Wikimedia external link, and a tiny corner mark on list thumbnails.

Owned photo leads (photo 1 — no badge, no credit). Swiping to photo 2 shows the kept stock photo, badged and credited (see the two hero artboards to the left). The badge overlays ONLY the fetched image; the credit line follows the active photo, so it isn't shown while the owned photo is up.

The mark distinguishes a fetched photo from the person's own. On the item list the contrast is real: Hasselblad + Technics are owned but not yet shot (stock photo, marked); Nikon + Stratocaster carry the person's own photo (no mark). Owned items are kept distinct from the wishlist samples (Leica M6, Fender Telecaster, Rega Planar 3), which live only on the wishlist. A wishlist item can never hold an owned photo, so its no-mark row is a not-yet-chosen placeholder (Vox). Wishlist rows gain a 52px thumbnail in 005 — flag this as a layout change.
